title: Darbuka (goblet drum)
summary: The darbuka is a goblet-shaped hand drum of Egypt, the Levant and Turkey, today usually pressed from metal. Held across the lap, it is played with both hands: the deep Dum in the middle of the head, the sharp Tek with the fingertips near the edge, and the light Ka with the other hand.
howToPlay: Three places on the head are lit: the centre for Dum, an inner ring for Tek and an outer ring for Ka. The hoop makes a Rim click.
A ring closes on the place to strike. The rhythms are played as a chain of Dum, Tek and Ka.
The cycles are called iqa'at: maqsum is the best known.
Say the names Dum, Tek and Ka as you play, in time with the lit places.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The three cycles are played in turn, each with its own count of beats to the bar.
heritageNote: Egyptian and Levantine players name their cycles, called iqa'at, by the arrangement of Dum and Tek. Maqsum and baladi are heard in dance music from Cairo to Beirut.
